title.narrative: Provision of early lifesaving health response to flood affected communities in Beletweyne, Hiran Region

description.narrative:
ltpgt
lt/pgtltp style="text-align:justifymso-prop-change:" class="MsoNormal"gtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black" lang="EN-US"gtSave the Children (SC) proposes to deliver lifesaving health support to vulnerable communities (including men, women, boys and girls) in Beledweyne district. These interventions are based on the 2023 allocation strategy and the proposed activities are well aligned with the 2023 Humanitarian Response Plan and Health cluster priorities. The project aims to reduce risk of disease outbreak (AWD/cholera and other communicable diseases) and its impact to the flood affected population. This will be achieved through establishment of well-equipped Cholera Treatment Centers (CTC) in Beledweyne and setting Oral Rehydration Points and Cholera Treatment Units (CTU) at strategic locations within the target settlements. SC will preposition cholera treatment supplies, procure reproductive health kits including rape kits and clean delivery kits, support infection prevention control (IPC), procure insecticide treated bed nets, train staff on cholera case management, clinical management of rape and surveillance, conduct risk communication and community engagement (RCCE) activities to reduce exposure risks to the susceptible population. SC will establish two satellite clinics to ensure continuity of essential primary health care services in line with the revised Essential Package of Health Services (EPHS) framework, including emergency and comprehensive obstetric care, compassionate care for survivors of Gender Based Violence (GBV), establish referral pathways for Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) linkages and refer critical medical/obstetric emergencies to higher facilities for secondary care. SC will also support provision of essential routine immunization services and management of childhood illnesses to reduce child morbidity and mortality. ltspan style="font-family: "arial, sans-serif", sans-serif" lang="EN-US"gtSC will closely coordinate with other cluster partners in the region in referral and linkages such as HINNA for shelter and non-food items (NFIs) for the displaced households. WASH cluster partners SC will work with include Action Aid, Action Against Disasters Somalia, Humanitarian Integrity for Women Action (HIWA) to provide clean water, sanitation services and hygiene promotion messaging. SC will also work with HIWA in the Integration of GBV and Protection services.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black" lang="EN-US"gtltspan style="font-family: "arial, sans-serif", sans-serif" lang="EN-US"gtltspan lang="EN-US"gt Through complementary support from Damal Cafimaad and Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance (BHA) projects, SC will ensure deployment of outbreak response teams, equitable access to WASH services by vulnerable groups such as the elderly, young children and people with disabilities, safety of children and dignity and privacy for women and girls. Additionally, beneficiaries will be sensitized on hygiene promotion measures with a focus on proper hand washing with soap, safe waste and excreta disposal and household (HH) water treatment and safe storage and build community resilience and increase sustainability of WASH services by enhancing the capacity of village level WASH management committees to manage, operate and maintain WASH facilities. Coordination with health and WASH clusters at national and state levels will be maintained, in addition to ongoing coordination with key actors in Hiran region. The project will address gender issues through collecting sex and age disaggregated data which will be analyzed to identify gaps, provide gender sensitive interventions, and ensure participation and empowerment of women. Protection of beneficiaries will be ensured during access and utilization of services seeking to reduce further risks.
lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="sceditor-nlf"gtltbrgt ltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: Arial, sans-serif color: black"gtltspan lang="EN-US" style="font-family: "arial, sans-serif", sans-serif"gtSC will ensure transparency to the affected populations by providing them with accessible and timely information on selection criteria for targeted assistance, organizational procedures and processes that affect them. SC will set-up accessible, confidential, and inclsuive feedback mechanisms for suggestions and complaints with a view to improve programming, understand community perceptions, promote beneficiary empowerment, and assist in reporting incidents. lt/spangtlt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgt
